newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Israel in dispute on Arafat-Netanyahu talks.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel in dispute on Arafat-Netanyahu talks.

text.p: A dispute over the wording of an Israeli-PLO written commitment to the Oslo peace agreement on Tuesday delayed a first meeting between Benjamin Netanyahu and Yasser Arafat, officials said.
Three days of talks have failed to fix a summit between the Israeli and Palestinian leaders, seen as vital for reviving their stalled self-rule agreement for the West Bank and Gaza.
"It is most unlikely Arafat will meet Netanyahu today," a Palestinian official said.
Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said the sides were making progress towards an agreement paving the way for a Netanyahu-Arafat meeting and the resumption of full-fledged peace negotiations.
But neither he nor Netanyahu would commit to a date.
"I'm going to disappoint you by repeating what I've said time and time again," Netanyahu told reporters.
"The meeting between Arafat and myself is not dependent on a calendar but on developments. I hope those developments will proceed productively so that we can have a productive meeting," he said.
PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat said contacts continued in an effort to resolve the one issue he said was delaying a meeting between Arafat and Netanyahu.
"President Arafat wants one thing from Mr. Netanyahu, that he honours the agreements and will implement them," Erekat said.
He and other PLO officials accused the Israelis of refusing to include the word "implementation" in a joint communique reaffirming their commitment to the 1993 Oslo autonomy accord.
Palestinians say Prime Minister Netanyahu is willing to commit himself to the principle of Oslo but not to its implementation at this stage.
"The Israelis are still delaying because they refuse to commit themselves to implementing agreements either verbally or in writing," Arafat's spokesman Nabil Abu Rdaineh said.
Erekat said he reached an understanding in talks on Monday with Netanyahu adviser and negotiator Dore Gold on all issues including Israel's commitment to implement peace deals.

Erekat told Reuters that both sides had agreed that the Arafat-Netanyahu meeting would be held on Tuesday afternoon. This agreement, he said, was retracted by a Netanyahu envoy during talks with Arafat in Gaza on Monday night.
"To our surprise another representative of the Israeli government came Monday night to President Arafat and said Mr. Gold was not authorised to make agreements," Erekat said.

"I say very clearly that the intention of this Israeli government is to renegotiate the agreements and to start from the beginning," Erekat said. "Netanyahu is not able to say he is committed to implementing the signed agreements, and then I think the peace process is at a very critical stage."

Israel and the PLO have been holding talks in a Tel Aviv apartment. Contacts continued into the night after Arafat threatened to seek international arbitration if Israeli-PLO attempts to resume peace talks faltered.
A spokesman for Netanyahu said Israel rejects arbitration and said the Palestinian leader was trying to put pressure on Israel during negotiations.
PLO officials have said they would not renegotiate agreements signed by former Labour prime minister Shimon Peres.
Netanyahu, who won election in May pledging not to trade occupied land for peace, has said he would only meet Arafat when he deems it necessary for Israel's security.
